🇲🇽🛢️ MEXICAN CRUDE IS KEEPING JAPAN'S REFINERIES RUNNING

With the Strait of Hormuz choked by the US-Iran war, Japan turned to Pemex: one million barrels of Mexican crude shipped to supply Cosmo Oil's refineries, sealed in a call between Sheinbaum and PM Takaichi. Per El Financiero, Tokyo moved to diversify away from Gulf supply the moment Hormuz closed — and Mexico, not Washington, was the reliable partner on the phone.

🇲🇽🌊 20 BILLION PESOS TO REVIVE THREE OF MEXICO'S MOST POISONED RIVERS

Sheinbaum's government is investing 20 billion pesos this term to clean the Atoyac, Lerma-Santiago and Tula rivers — decades of untreated sewage and illegal industrial discharge — with treatment plants, wetlands and reforestation for 25 million people across 10 states and 61 municipalities. "It's very intense work," she said. Forty years of neoliberal dumping; the 4T is dredging it out.

🚨🇲🇽 MEXICO TOLD THE CIA TO LEAVE — AND THEY LEFT

Sheinbaum confirmed her government formally asked Washington to withdraw unauthorized CIA agents operating clandestinely in Chihuahua: "when we asked them to leave our country... they did leave." Roughly 250 foreign agents are registered in Mexico — all bound by the Constitution and the National Security Law, all filing monthly reports. Sovereignty enforced through diplomacy, not headlines.

🔥🇲🇽 THE JUDGE WHO REOPENED THE PIPELINE FOR MEXICO'S BIGGEST FUEL-THEFT RING

Federal judge Juan Pablo Gómez Fierro handed Ingemar SA an amparo forcing the Energy Ministry to restore the fuel-import permit AMLO's government had cancelled — a network that cost the treasury 4.456 billion pesos, moved 15 million liters of illegal gasoline and used 162 rail tankers to dodge taxes. The same judge later fought judicial reform, then walked off the bench.

🚨🇲🇽 MEXICO EYES A CUT OF THE $15 BILLION WASHINGTON SEIZED FROM 'EL MAYO'

A Brooklyn court hit Ismael 'El Mayo' Zambada with life plus a $15 billion forfeiture — about 270 billion pesos. Sheinbaum says she'll ask the FGR whether Mexico can claim part of it as damage reparation: "We're going to ask the Prosecutor to review... normally this is done." The cartel's profits were extracted here — the reparations belong here too.

🇲🇽🏥 MEXICO IS BUILDING 152 HOSPITALS — 181 BILLION PESOS, NO PRIVATIZATION

While Washington debates gutting Medicaid, Sheinbaum's government is putting 181 billion pesos into 152 public hospital projects this term — 50 brand-new hospitals, 47 expansions, lifting public beds from 96,966 to 106,105. 39 projects already finished in the first 22 months. Health as a right, not a market.

REUTERS: Chinese car sales in Mexico surge despite new tariffs
July 20, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Reuters: Chinese-brand car sales in Mexico jumped ~30% in the first half of 2026 to 17% of the market — flagged as a "contentious issue" hanging over the US-Mexico trade talks. 🇲🇽

Mexico's own trade ministry says Chinese vehicle imports actually fell 43% this year — the strong sales are pre-tariff inventory clearing, not a flood Washington can pin on Mexico.

• Chinese brands: 17% of new sales (137,525 units), up from 14%
• From under 1% market share in 2020 to 17% in 2026
• Deputy trade minister: imports down 43%; sales reflect "inventory built up before" the tariffs

SMALL WARS JOURNAL: Hybrid Violence in Mexico
July 16, 2026 | 🟡

📰 A US security journal reframes Mexican cartels as "hybrid violent actors" exercising "state capture" and "parallel governance" — language that inflates criminal profit-groups into sovereignty-level threats. 🔍

The same authors admit the 2025 terrorist designation changed little on the ground — cartels just fragmented and leaned on proxies — and note Mexico rejected US military intervention outright.

• "operate at the intersection of organized crime, paramilitary force... and state capture, challenging national sovereignty"
• the FTO designation was "partly legal, partly strategic, and partly theatrical"
• its "principal effect... was not restriction but adaptive restructuring"

REUTERS/US NEWS: US, Mexico resume USMCA talks as Trump hits Canada with new tariffs
July 21, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Washington reopens bilateral USMCA talks with Mexico — crediting its "pragmatic," no-retaliation approach — the same week it slaps Canada with 50% tariffs on ~$20B in goods. 🇲🇽 Negotiate quietly, keep your seat; push back, get punished.

The "pragmatism" Mexico is praised for is accepting the 25% auto and 50% steel tariffs it is still trying to lift — without retaliating.

• USTR Greer: Mexico deserves credit for its "pragmatic" approach
• Amb. Lazzeri: "Every moment... we are losing competitiveness, market share and investment"
• Canada "largely sidelined"; Carney says the tariffs "violated" the pact

🇲🇽🏭 MEXICO'S TARIFFS ON ASIA ARE WORKING: IMPORTS DOWN 23.2%, CHINA DOWN 28.4%

Six months in, Mexico's tariffs on countries without trade deals are reshaping trade: imports across 1,463 tariff lines fell 23.2% (from $15.4B to $11.8B) Jan–May, with China down 28.4%, auto parts −39.5%, and steel −30%, per El Financiero. Economy Secretary Ebrard projected over 70 billion pesos in revenue with barely 0.2% inflation impact. Industrial policy with a spine.
